transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um... I guess I came in because I've been dealing with some things that are probably just stress from work, but I wanted to make sure I'm handling it the right way. Is it okay if I just explain a little bit? 

I'm a personal financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and... well, for a while now, I’ve been kind of convinced that certain people in the local arts and finance circles are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. I know how that sounds, and I really don't want to seem unreasonable, but it just feels like they're sending me little signals. Just through things like event invitations, or the topics chosen for panels, or even who ends up sitting near me at dinners. 

I keep telling myself it could just be a coincidence, and I really try to be rational and just focus on my work, but... I just can’t really let it go. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to talk to someone about it.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, confident, or like your thoughts were racing ahead of your speech? Times when you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt great?

No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I try to stay positive and, you know, keep my energy up for my clients, but... I wouldn't say I've ever felt unusually energetic or anything like that. And I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get a solid seven or eight hours, I'm just... I'm not at my best the next day. 

I always try to be really careful about my sleep schedule so I can be professional. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just... I really haven't experienced anything like what you're describing. I'm pretty even-keeled, mostly. Is that okay?
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?

Oh, um, no. No, nothing like that. I know what I said earlier about the... the signals and the arts circle might sound a little, well, unusual, but I promise I'm not seeing things that aren't real. 

The things I notice are just actual things, you know? Like a real physical invitation, or a real conversation at a dinner. I've never heard voices or seen anything that wasn't actually right there in the room with me. 

I try really hard to keep a clear head for my job, so I feel like I'd notice if my mind was playing tricks on me like that. I hope that makes sense? I just want to assure you I'm completely grounded in that way. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful.

When you think about these people tracking your clients and sending you signals, how certain are you that this is actually happening? Do you ever doubt it, or do you feel completely convinced it's real?

Um... well, like I was saying before, I really do try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence. I know how it sounds, and I don't want to come across as irrational or anything. I pride myself on being very logical for my clients. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to admit this... I am pretty convinced it's actually happening. It's just... the way these specific people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati operate. I really feel they are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. And those little signals I mentioned—the specific event invitations, the panel topics, exactly who ends up sitting near me at dinners—it just feels too deliberate to be random. 

So... I guess I do try to doubt it, because I want to be sensible and professional, but I just can't really let it go. It feels very real to me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it in a way that's helpful for you, I really don't want to sound difficult.
How long have you been having these thoughts about people tracking your clients and sending you signals? When did this first start?

Um... let me think. I guess... well, it hasn't been that long, really. I'd say maybe... about two months? Give or take? 

It's not like it's been happening my whole career or anything like that. I've always been very focused and professional. It just sort of... started recently, these past couple of months, where I started noticing the patterns with the invitations and the tracking. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too distracted from my work? Two months isn't that long in the grand scheme of things, right? I'm still doing a really good job for my clients, I promise. I just wanted to be honest with you about the timeline. Is that the kind of detail you needed?
Besides the tracking and the signals you mentioned, have you noticed any changes in how you speak, organize your thoughts, or go about your daily activities over these past two months?

Um... no, no, nothing like that at all. I really pride myself on being very organized, especially with my job. My thoughts are completely clear, and I'm speaking just the same as I always have. 

I haven't had any trouble with my daily routine, either. I'm still getting up, going to the office, managing my clients' portfolios... everything is completely normal on that front. I really wouldn't let anything interfere with my work or how I present myself, you know? 

I just... I want to make sure you know I'm still functioning perfectly fine. I'm not falling apart or anything. Everything else is completely on track. Does that sound okay? I hope I'm not coming across like I'm disorganized or... or losing my grip on things.
Over these past two months, have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family, or have you withdrawn from social activities you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I really try to keep up with everyone, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just hiding away or being anti-social. I know how important relationships are, especially in my line of work. 

But... I guess, if I'm being totally honest—and I hope it's okay to admit this—I just haven't had that same... spark? lately. Like, I still get all my work done, I really do, just maybe in pieces. And I might leave a few routine client follow-ups sitting a little longer than I normally would. I'm still taking good care of them, though! 

Outside of the office, I guess I have skipped a few things. I usually go to these jazz nights, or play pickup basketball with some guys, but lately I've just been skipping them... and I don't really feel much about missing out, to be honest. And when my friends ask what's going on with me, I've just been giving really short answers. It's definitely not that I don't care about them! It's just... talking kind of feels like a lot more effort than it should right now. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad friend, or like I'm getting lazy. I'm really trying my best to keep everything balanced. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering this right.

Before these past two months started, would you say you were functioning well at work and socially—meeting all your client needs promptly, staying engaged with friends and hobbies? Or have you always tended to feel this way, even before the tracking thoughts began?

Oh, no, definitely not always like this. Before a couple of months ago, I was... um, I was doing really, really well. I promise. 

I've always been very on top of my game at work. You know, as a financial advisor, you really have to be, and I always took a lot of pride in that. I was meeting all my clients' needs right away, never leaving anything sitting on my desk. I've always had a really great track record.

And socially, too! I was usually the one getting people together for the jazz nights, or making sure we had enough guys for basketball. I was very engaged and active with my friends. 

It's really just been this recent... well, since I started noticing the signals and the tracking, that things got a little slower. But before that, everything was completely normal. I really hope that shows I'm normally a very reliable, outgoing person? I'd hate for you to think this is just how I've always been, or that I'm naturally a slacker. Does that help clear up the timeline a bit for you?
Before these past two months, did you ever have any unusual beliefs or suspicions about people—even minor ones—or did you ever feel like things around you had special meanings directed at you?

Um... no, definitely not. I've never had anything like that happen before. 

I've always been a very, um, grounded person. I mean, working in finance, you really have to base everything on facts and data, right? So I never had any reason to be suspicious of people, and I definitely never thought random things had hidden meanings or were directed at me. 

I really want to be clear that before these last couple of months, my mind was totally... well, normal. Just focused on my clients and my life. I hope that makes sense? I just really don't want you to think I've been secretly paranoid my whole life or something. I've always prided myself on being very rational and level-headed. Does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I usually am.
